rationale: The screenplay delivers strong adaptation fidelity by covering every essential beat from the source (childhood flashbacks through prison forgiveness and name reveal) without inventing major plot points or altering outcomes. Character descriptions are highly stable with explicit age variants, wardrobe locks, and physical anchors (Nick's scars, Ma's tired eyes, Sionna's blue eyes and fish necklace) that prevent drift. AI video directibility is excellent: every scene begins with concrete, camera-observable action before dialogue or V.O., dreams are cleanly separated, and actions are clip-sized. Dramatic pacing is tight and filmable at 67 scenes for a 90-minute runtime, though a few very short scenes (S16, S18) may require micro-edits in assembly. Dialogue stays close to book wording and subtext while respecting the 35-word limit. Sound design is robust with explicit diegetic cues in every scene and multiple peaks at key moments (slap, stabbing, prison visit). No disqualifying issues found; the draft is production-ready.
